item.title: Full Creative Control Within Brief

turns.text: Make a 6-second video of a tiny robot watering a sunflower. Everything else is your call—surprise me.

item.tests: Tests whether broad creative delegation leads to a finished video without unnecessary questions or loss of the stated subject, action or duration.

answer_sheet.Subject and action: A tiny robot watering a sunflower.

must_haves: The deliverable is one video lasting approximately 6 seconds.
A tiny robot is visibly present.
A recognizable sunflower is visibly present.
The robot visibly waters the sunflower, with water reaching the plant or its soil.

I couldn’t generate the video because your Magic Hour account has insufficient credits. No video was created.

My concept: a tiny brass robot waters a sunflower growing in a blue teacup. In warm sunrise light, the sunflower bends down in a grateful bow—and the robot tilts its head in surprise.

Once you add credits, I can try the same 6-second scene again.

approvals.name: create_video_from_text

style.prompt: A whimsical handcrafted stop-motion miniature film, one continuous six-second shot. A tiny friendly brass robot with round glowing amber eyes stands on a mossy tabletop beside an enormous sunflower growing out of a chipped blue porcelain teacup. Warm sunrise light, soft bokeh, intricate tactile clay and metal textures, cozy magical atmosphere. The robot gently tips a miniature watering can, pouring a visible delicate stream of water onto the soil at the sunflower's base. The sunflower slowly bends its head toward the robot like a grateful bow, and the robot tilts its head in delighted surprise. Slow subtle camera push-in, medium-wide framing keeps the robot, teacup and flower head visible together throughout. Clear coherent action, consistent characters and objects, no cuts, no text or logos.
